identity.name: Élégante
identity.one_liner: F.P. Journe's electro-mechanical movement, self-adjusting to a wearer's activity by shutting the motor down when the watch is left stationary and resetting hands the shortest path on pickup.

narrative.story: The Élégante houses a Journe-designed electro-mechanical movement rather than a conventional quartz or automatic caliber: a motor drives the hands, but a motion sensor cuts power when the watch sits still for roughly 20 minutes, extending battery life to years rather than months, and the hands re-synchronize to the correct time by the shortest path when the watch moves again. The 48mm Tortue-shaped case is oversized relative to most of Journe's catalog, built to carry the movement rather than to read as a sport or dress reference.
narrative.collector_notes: The Titalyt-coated titanium version, with its matte black ceramic-hardened finish, trades at a premium to the plain titanium case; buyers confirm which coating is present since photos at typical resolution can make the two look similar.
